# SK7050 — A warning-disable pragma has no justification

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

The source suppresses one or more diagnostics without telling the next reader why the warning is wrong here.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Maintainability |
| Default severity | warning |
| Scope | Syntax |
| Needs a compilation | no |
| Fix | no |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 2.0 |

## Why

A local pragma is an explicit exception to a repository rule. Without a reason, nobody can distinguish a deliberate exception from a temporary silencing, decide whether it is still necessary, or safely remove it. The rule accepts a meaningful trailing or immediately preceding comment and never manufactures one, because a generated justification would be worse than none.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
#pragma warning disable CA1822
```

Write:

```csharp
#pragma warning disable CA1822 // Called by reflection through the instance.
```

## When it does not fire

A comment farther away than the immediately preceding nonblank line is not associated with the pragma. The rule checks presence and rejects blank/TODO/FIXME placeholders; it cannot prove that the prose is truthful.

- `dotnet_diagnostic.SK7050.severity`
